words.definition: to move slowly while making a puffing or thumping sound, like an engine
words.example: The old train began to chug up the hill.
examples: He listened as the train chugged through the countryside.
We heard the boat chug across the lake before we could see it.
The tractor chugged along the muddy field all morning.

words.definition: something with circular ends and straight sides
words.example: A soup can is shaped like a cylinder.
examples: Two objects in my home that are cylinders are water bottles and candles.
The inventor rolled the paper into a cylinder to make a tube.
Each cylinder in the engine moves up and down very fast.

words.definition: a huge failure
words.example: The first version of the machine was a flop.
examples: One of his ideas turned out to be a complete flop, and nobody wanted to buy it.
Everyone said the movie would be a hit, but it turned out to be a flop.
His science project was a flop because the battery died.

words.definition: a small electronic device or machine
words.example: She invented a gadget that peels apples in ten seconds.
examples: The most useful gadget in my pencil bag is a mechanical pencil because I can write and draw quickly.
One gadget I can't live without is a smartwatch because I rely on it for communication.
My uncle loves every new kitchen gadget he sees in the store.

words.definition: producing light from a glowing wire inside a bulb
words.example: The incandescent bulb glowed warmly in the dark room.
examples: One evening, he worked under an incandescent light bulb that filled his workshop with a warm glow.
I used to have an incandescent light bulb at home, but it became too hot, so we replaced it with LED bulbs.
Edison worked for years to make an incandescent light that would last.

words.definition: a train engine that pulls train cars
words.example: The locomotive pulled twenty cars across the bridge.
examples: He watched the powerful locomotive pull the train cars down the tracks.
Steam poured from the locomotive as it left the station.
The museum has a locomotive that is over one hundred years old.

words.definition: a document to protect an invention
words.example: The inventor received a patent for her new machine.
examples: After months of hard work, he finished his new machine and applied for a patent so that no one could copy his invention.
Without a patent, anyone could copy the design and sell it.
Thomas Edison held more than one thousand patents in his lifetime.

words.definition: to work unevenly with popping noises
words.example: The old engine began to sputter and then stopped.
examples: The candle sputtered in the wind before it went out.
The car sputtered twice, then finally started.
The broken radio sputtered and crackled all afternoon.

words.definition: an early machine that played recorded sound from a spinning disk or cylinder
words.example: Grandpa still plays old records on his phonograph.
examples: As he worked, he listened to music on an old phonograph that had belonged to his grandfather.
Edison's phonograph was the first machine that could record and play back a voice.
The phonograph had a large horn that made the music louder.

words.definition: a large room where people gather to watch events
words.example: The whole school met in the auditorium for the concert.
examples: Chingshin Academy has an auditorium where the students perform shows.
The auditorium was so full that some parents had to stand in the back.
Our play will be performed in the new auditorium next Friday.

words.definition: the best or most skilled members in a group
words.example: Only elite athletes are chosen for the national team.
examples: The elite Navy SEAL teams spend years training to prepare for challenging military missions.
An elite group of scientists gathered in the laboratory to conduct a very difficult experiment.
She joined an elite group of pilots who fly the newest jets.

words.definition: someone who checks something carefully for problems
words.example: The inspector checked every wire before the lights were turned on.
examples: An inspector would visit a school to make sure the building is safe and the rules are followed.
A food inspector visits the restaurant twice a year.
The building inspector said the new stairs were safe to use.

words.definition: a goal
words.example: Our objective is to finish the robot before the science fair.
examples: My objective for this semester is to improve my English grade.
The main objective of the project was to bring clean water to the village.
She wrote her objective at the top of the page: read one book a week.

words.definition: to take a picture with a camera; a picture taken with a camera
words.example: Dad likes to photograph birds in the park.
examples: I photographed all the different animals I saw with my new camera.
When she was on holiday, she photographed all the beautiful places she saw.
The reporter photographed the windmill from every side.

words.definition: well-known and respected because of high quality or success
words.example: He won a prestigious award for his invention.
examples: She got the most prestigious award in the competition because she was the best performer in all the events.
The award is very prestigious because only the best jump rope team can win it.
She was invited to study at a prestigious university.

words.definition: to focus on one particular subject, skill, or type of work
words.example: The doctor decided to specialize in heart surgery.
examples: The research center is known for helping scientists who specialize in studying rare animals.
Doctors might choose to specialize in one type of medicine so they can become experts at helping certain patients.
This shop specializes in repairing old bicycles.

words.definition: when something is done a certain way for a long time
words.example: The villagers wore traditional clothes for the festival.
examples: Traditional windmills were made of wood and cloth.
My grandmother cooks a traditional meal every New Year.
The school still holds its traditional sports day every October.

words.definition: very poor
words.example: The impoverished family could not afford to buy a lamp.
examples: Many impoverished villages have no electricity at all.
The drought left the farmers impoverished and hungry.
William built a windmill to help his impoverished village pump water.

words.definition: to bring water to dry land through pipes, ditches, or channels so crops can grow
words.example: The farmers dug ditches to irrigate their fields.
examples: A windmill pumped water to irrigate the corn.
The new pipes irrigated the whole garden in an hour.
Without rain, the village needed a way to irrigate its crops.

words.definition: to move something skillfully or carefully into a position
words.example: The pilot had to maneuver the plane around the storm.
examples: She maneuvered the wheelchair through the narrow doorway.
The captain maneuvered the ship into the small harbor.
The players maneuvered their chairs quickly to block the shot.

words.definition: the act of speeding up
words.example: The race car's acceleration pushed the driver back into his seat.
examples: After the science experiment, they discussed the acceleration of the moving car.
It is convenient to have strong acceleration in a car because it can speed up quickly.
Gravity causes the acceleration of a falling apple.

words.definition: a condition or situation that affects what happens
words.example: Bad weather was one circumstance that delayed the flight.
examples: Due to unexpected circumstances, we had to cancel our outdoor activity.
Under no circumstance should you touch the hot wire.
The inventor succeeded despite every difficult circumstance.

words.definition: to form an idea or plan in your mind
words.example: It is hard to conceive of a world without electricity.
examples: Abigail conceived an idea for a robot that would do her homework for her.
People conceive new ideas for solving problems by thinking the problem over and over.
Who first conceived the idea of a wheelchair race?

words.definition: something you give or do to help make something happen
words.example: Her biggest contribution to the team was her patience.
examples: Each one of the team members made a huge contribution to the project by sharing ideas.
My contribution to the party would be a big box of cookies.
The scientist's contribution changed how we study the stars.

words.definition: respected and admired because of great achievements
words.example: A distinguished scientist spoke to our class.
examples: A distinguished professor might dress very professionally in a suit and tie.
The distinguished inventor received a medal from the president.
She had a long and distinguished career as a doctor.

words.definition: clearly or obviously, based on what can be seen or known
words.example: The bridge was evidently too weak to hold the truck.
examples: The students were evidently upset about the end-of-year party being canceled.
The other scientists are evidently scared because the mad scientist blew up the lab.
The dog had evidently found the cookies, because the jar was empty.

words.definition: a sudden strong desire to do something
words.example: On an impulse, he bought a kite at the market.
examples: An impulse I need to control in class is the feeling of standing up and walking around when I am bored.
She felt a sudden impulse to jump into the cold lake.
Try not to act on every impulse when you are angry.

words.definition: having a strong feeling of excitement or love for something
words.example: She is passionate about protecting sea turtles.
examples: The teacher was so passionate about history that she dressed up as different characters from the past.
The mad scientist is so passionate about science that he blows up the lab.
He gave a passionate speech about clean energy.

words.definition: the first model of something, made to test an idea before it is made in large numbers
words.example: The team built a prototype of the robot out of cardboard.
examples: The first prototype crashed, so they made a stronger one.
Engineers test a prototype many times before selling the real product.
Captain Arsenio's prototype of a flying machine never left the ground.

words.definition: unusual or odd in behavior or appearance
words.example: The eccentric inventor wore a hat covered with springs.
examples: Our eccentric neighbor paints his fence a new color every week.
People laughed at Captain Arsenio's eccentric flying machines.
The eccentric scientist kept a pet snake in his desk drawer.
